resources.name: SoundBetter
resources.description: Music production marketplace with 50,000+ vetted music professionals across 176 countries. Find session musicians, producers, singers, and engineers by reviews, price, location, and credits. Free to browse and hire; pros set their own rates.
resources.cost: Free to browse, post jobs, and hire; service prices set by pros (~$100–$2,000+). Clients pay no platform fee; SoundBetter takes a small commission from pros.

resources.name: AirGigs
resources.description: Marketplace for hiring session musicians, vocalists, and audio engineers for remote recording. Launched in 2012, it features detailed artist profiles, audio samples, and secure escrow payments.
resources.cost: Free to browse. Buyers pay 4.7% service fee. Sellers pay 10–15% commission.
highlights: Open marketplace with a light seller profile review

resources.name: Fiverr — Music & Audio
resources.description: Global freelance marketplace with a large Music & Audio category. Find session guitarists, drummers, bassists, vocalists, and more. Filter by instrument, genre, budget, and delivery time.
resources.cost: Services start at ~$5. Average session musician gig: $50–$400. Buyers pay 5.5% + $3.50 small-order fee on orders under $200.

resources.name: Musiversal
resources.description: Subscription-based platform for live, directed recording sessions with world-class musicians. Collaborate in real time, give feedback instantly, and receive takes within 15 minutes.
resources.cost: Unlimited membership $249/mo (cancel or pause anytime); new members join via a monthly waitlist. Add-ons such as a full mix cost extra.
highlights: All instruments: drums, guitar, bass, keys, strings, horns, vocals
Tracks made on it include a Latin Grammy winner

resources.name: Supreme Tracks
resources.description: Curated roster of professional session musicians who record in pro studios. A session producer reviews your demo, translates your vision, and handpicks the right player.
resources.cost: $150–$225 per instrument depending on genre, length, and number of songs.
highlights: Handpicked musicians matched to your genre

resources.name: BeatStars
resources.description: The largest beat-selling marketplace connecting producers and artists. Browse, preview, and license beats with instant delivery. Supports exclusive and non-exclusive licenses.
resources.cost: Free to browse. Beat prices set by producers (typically $20–$500+). 12% buyer service fee on Marketplace purchases.
highlights: Largest producer community in the industry

resources.name: Airbit
resources.description: Beat marketplace focused on producer-friendly pricing. Upload and sell beats with 0% seller commission and no buyer fees on the Marketplace. Supports custom beat stores and licensing.
resources.cost: Free Basic plan (up to 20 beats, Marketplace only). Platinum $19.99/mo or $7.99/mo billed yearly (unlimited beats + your own beat store). 0% seller commission.
highlights: 0% seller commission, even on the free plan

resources.name: SoundBetter — Producers
resources.description: Find and hire music producers through the SoundBetter marketplace. Filter by genre, credits, reviews, and budget. Work directly with the producer through the platform.
resources.cost: Free to browse and hire; producer rates vary (~$200–$5,000+). Clients pay no platform fee; pros pay a small commission.
highlights: Same trust system as SoundBetter session musicians

resources.name: Splice — Sounds & Samples
resources.description: Massive royalty-free sample library used by 10M+ producers. Access millions of loops, one-shots, presets, and MIDI packs. Rent-to-own plugins like Serum.
resources.cost: Free tier available. Sounds+ $12.99/mo (100 credits), Creator $19.99/mo (200 credits), Creator+ $39.99/mo (500 credits). Rent-to-own plugins such as Serum 2 ($9.99/mo) and RC-20 ($4.99/mo).
highlights: In-DAW integration with Ableton, Studio One

resources.name: Tracklib
resources.description: Legal sample-clearance platform. Browse a catalog of real, original recordings and license samples with pre-cleared rights for your productions.
resources.cost: Free to browse and preview. Subscription from $14.99/mo or $119.99/yr (375 credits/mo); sample clearance included with no upfront license fees. Revenue share applies to releases.

resources.name: SoundBetter — Mixing Engineers
resources.description: Browse and hire mixing engineers from SoundBetter's vetted roster. Filter by genre specialty, credits, reviews, and budget. Includes Grammy-winning engineers.
resources.cost: Free to browse and hire; rates set by engineers. Clients pay no platform fee; pros pay a small commission.
highlights: Engineers with major label credits available

resources.name: LANDR
resources.description: AI-powered mastering platform. Upload your track and get an instant master. Also includes distribution to streaming platforms, sample packs, and a mastering plugin for your DAW. Note: AI mastering is solid; the distribution side has reported account-suspension complaints — best to use for mastering only.
resources.cost: Essentials $13/mo (MP3 masters + distribution). Standard $20/mo (3 WAV/mo). Pro $25/mo (unlimited WAV + HD WAV). Yearly: $99, $144, or $300 (Pro yearly currently 36% off). Or $10 per single master.
highlights: Unlimited free previews before you pay
Includes distribution to Spotify, Apple Music, etc.
DAW mastering plugin on Standard and Pro tiers

resources.name: eMastered
resources.description: AI mastering service co-founded by a Grammy-winning engineer (Smith Carlson, Taylor Swift's 1989). More mastering controls than LANDR — adjust EQ, compression, stereo width, and loudness. Note: mastering quality is strong, but cancellation/refund process has documented billing issues — review subscription terms carefully.
resources.cost: $49/mo month-to-month, or $19/mo on a 1-year commitment ($156/yr if paid upfront). Includes unlimited high-res WAV downloads. 14-day refund if fewer than 4 downloads.

resources.name: AirGigs — Mixing & Mastering
resources.description: Hire mixing and mastering engineers on the AirGigs marketplace. Compare profiles, listen to before/after samples, and read reviews from other artists.
resources.cost: Service prices set by engineers. Buyers pay 4.7% fee.
highlights: Wide price range for all budgets

resources.name: Fiverr — Mixing & Mastering
resources.description: Find mixing and mastering engineers on Fiverr's freelance marketplace. Good for budget-conscious projects with fast turnaround needs.
resources.cost: Services from ~$10. Fiverr Pro (vetted) engineers available at higher rates.

resources.name: BandLab — Mastering
resources.description: Free AI mastering built into the BandLab platform. Upload your finished mix and get an instant master. Part of a free, cloud-based DAW with 100M+ users.
resources.cost: Free (basic AI mastering). Membership tier available for premium features.

resources.name: SoundBetter — Singers & Songwriters
resources.description: Find male and female session singers, topliners, and songwriters on SoundBetter. Filter by genre, vocal range, and budget. Includes background vocalists and topliner writers.
resources.cost: Free to browse, post jobs, and hire; vocalist rates vary (~$100–$2,000+). SoundBetter's commission is paid by the provider, not the client.

resources.name: Fiverr — Singers & Songwriters
resources.description: Hire session singers, background vocalists, jingle singers, and songwriters on Fiverr. Wide range of genres and pricing. Filter by vocal style, gender, and language.
resources.cost: Services from ~$20. Average vocal track: $50–$200+.
highlights: Huge selection of vocal styles and languages
Fiverr Pro tier of vetted vocalists

resources.name: AirGigs — Vocalists
resources.description: Hire session singers, background vocalists, and songwriters on AirGigs. Listen to audio samples, read reviews, and work through secure escrow payments.
resources.cost: Service prices set by vocalists. Buyers pay a 4.7% service fee ($5 minimum).

resources.name: Kompoz
resources.description: Online music collaboration platform for asynchronous songwriting. Upload stems, invite collaborators worldwide, and build songs together. Built-in royalty split tracking.
resources.cost: Free Starter plan. Paid plans $5–$20/mo ($49–$199/yr) add WAV/AIF uploads and more private projects.
highlights: 10+ years as a leading collaboration platform
Community forums and groups by genre/instrument

resources.name: ProCollabs
resources.description: Online music collaboration platform with a manually verified membership. Share projects, find vocalists and songwriters, and collaborate across borders.
resources.cost: Free to join (manually verified).

resources.name: BandLab
resources.description: Free cloud-based DAW and social music platform with 100M+ users. Create, collaborate with up to 50 people per project, and share music — all from your browser or phone.
resources.cost: Free (all core features). Optional Pro and Max memberships add AI tools, pro features, and distribution.
highlights: Free multi-track recording, mixing, and mastering

resources.name: BandMix
resources.description: The largest musician classifieds site for finding local band members, session players, and music industry professionals. Search by location, instrument, genre, and experience level. Note: some users report renewal billing after cancellation — disable auto-renew when signing up.
resources.cost: Free account (limited). Premier: $12.95/mo, $33.95/3mo, or $99.95/yr ($8.33/mo).
highlights: Digital Auditions feature contacts 100 relevant musicians
Musician, Band, and Industry account types

resources.name: Soundtrap
resources.description: Cloud DAW built for real-time collaboration. Multiple users can work on the same track simultaneously with video chat. Includes loops, instruments, and podcasting tools.
resources.cost: Free tier available. Paid plans $11.99–$20.99/mo (7-day free trial).
highlights: Real-time simultaneous collaboration with video chat
New sound packs every two weeks

resources.name: Splice — Community
resources.description: Splice's free community hub on Discord hosts beat battles, remix contests, and producer networking. Members connect, share music, collaborate, and join creative challenges; no Splice subscription needed.
resources.cost: Free (Discord community). Splice subscription from $12.99/mo for samples and tools.
highlights: Free to join — no Splice subscription required
Beat battles with major producers (Murda Beatz, Chromeo)

resources.name: ASCAP
resources.description: American Society of Composers, Authors, and Publishers. Non-profit PRO representing 20M+ musical works. Collects performance royalties from radio, TV, live venues, and streaming for songwriters and publishers.
resources.cost: Free to join as a writer; publisher fee waived when joining as writer and publisher together (temporary policy). No annual dues. Member-owned.
highlights: Airport and hotel discounts for members
Join one PRO only — cannot also be BMI member

resources.name: BMI
resources.description: Broadcast Music, Inc. The largest US PRO, representing 1.5M+ songwriters, composers, and publishers and 25M+ musical works. Collects and distributes performance royalties for songwriters and publishers.
resources.cost: Free to join as a songwriter. No membership fee.
highlights: Free to join — no fees for songwriters
Songwriting camps and app subscriptions for members
Good first choice for indie songwriters

resources.name: SESAC
resources.description: Selective, invitation-only PRO. Much smaller roster than ASCAP/BMI (15,000+ affiliated songwriters, composers, and publishers; 1.5M+ songs). Focus on high-profile writers in TV, film, and major releases.
resources.cost: Invitation only. No public fee structure.
highlights: Notable members: Adele, Bob Dylan, Neil Diamond

resources.name: SoundExchange
resources.description: Non-profit that collects digital performance royalties for sound recordings (not compositions). Covers satellite radio (SiriusXM), internet radio (Pandora non-interactive), and other non-interactive digital streams.
resources.cost: Free to register.
highlights: Collects royalties ASCAP/BMI do not cover
Pays featured artists (45%), labels (50%), and session musicians (5%)
Register even if not getting digital radio play — collects back-royalties
Does NOT cover Spotify/Apple Music interactive streams

resources.name: The MLC (Mechanical Licensing Collective)
resources.description: Non-profit created by the Music Modernization Act. Administers blanket mechanical licenses for streaming services and distributes mechanical royalties to songwriters and publishers in the US.
resources.cost: Free. Fully funded by streaming services (Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon, etc.).
highlights: Collects mechanical royalties from all major streaming platforms
Search their Missing Member Lookup for unclaimed royalties

resources.name: Songtrust
resources.description: Global publishing administrator that registers your songs with 65+ collection societies across 240 countries and collects your publishing royalties. You retain 100% copyright ownership.
resources.cost: One-time $100 setup fee per songwriter. 15% commission on performance royalties; 20% on mechanical royalties.
highlights: No delivery obligations or advance requirements
~150K streams to break even on setup fee

resources.name: Ari's Take
resources.description: Comprehensive music business blog and podcast by Ari Herstand, author of "How to Make It in the New Music Business." Covers royalties, collaboration, sync licensing, touring, and career strategy.
resources.cost: Blog and podcast: Free. Ari's Take Academy courses: Paid (varies).
highlights: Praised by Forbes as "The poster child of DIY music"
Covers collaboration, splits, PROs, and sync in depth

resources.name: DIY Musician (CD Baby Blog)
resources.description: Long-running blog and podcast by CD Baby with hundreds of actionable articles on music promotion, releasing music, royalties, and career development for independent musicians.
resources.cost: Free (blog, podcast, and newsletter).
highlights: One of the most respected indie music resources
Covers release strategies, analytics, and promotion
DIY Musician Podcast archive (no new episodes since Oct 2024)

resources.name: Bandzoogle Blog
resources.description: Advice, inspiration, and practical resources for independent musicians. Covers marketing, website design, merchandise, revenue diversification, and music career strategies.
resources.cost: Free (blog).
highlights: Practical, actionable advice for indie artists
Covers merch, marketing, and website strategy

resources.name: Soundfly
resources.description: Online music school with free and premium courses across production, songwriting, theory, and music business. Free courses include royalty collection, home recording, and touring guides.
resources.cost: Free courses available. Subscription $12/mo or $96/yr unlocks all premium courses.
highlights: Free courses on royalties, recording, and touring
Premium courses taught by Kimbra, RJD2, Kiefer
Flypaper blog with additional free articles

resources.name: Hypebot
resources.description: Daily music industry news, insights, and analysis read by 30,000+ professionals. Covers music tech, artist marketing, live music, and industry trends with a focus on independent artists.
resources.cost: Free.
highlights: Strong coverage of music tech and AI in music

resources.name: Ari's Take Academy
resources.description: Paid course platform from Ari Herstand covering royalty registration, sync licensing, touring, and release strategy. Includes community access, live Q&As, and peer feedback.
resources.cost: Paid courses (pricing varies by course).
highlights: Step-by-step courses on royalties, sync, and touring
Community of musicians and industry professionals
Students often collaborate with each other

resources.name: Splice — Skills & Blog
resources.description: Free tutorials and articles on music production, sampling, and creative workflows. Skills platform offers in-depth production courses for subscribers.
resources.cost: Blog: Free. Skills tutorials included with Splice Creator plans (from $19.99/mo).

resources.name: Pibox
resources.description: Audio review and collaboration platform purpose-built for music production workflows. Leave time-stamped feedback directly on a track's waveform for organized async collaboration. Redesigned its iOS app in December 2025. Used by major media teams including Universal, Sony, and Epidemic Sound. Features AI tagging for organization. Raised $1.2M in November 2024.
resources.cost: Free plan (2 users, 1 GB); paid from $10/user/mo ($9/user/mo billed annually)
highlights: Used by Sony, Universal, and Epidemic Sound

resources.name: Lutefish
resources.description: ⚠️ HARDWARE-REQUIRED REAL-TIME JAMMING PLATFORM — Not a pure software collaboration tool. Minnesota-based platform launched November 2024. Lutefish Stream is a plug-and-play hardware device (cost ~$250) connecting via Ethernet to a router, enabling real-time audio streaming with latency as low as 30–35ms for musicians up to 500 miles apart. Backed by Wenger Corporation (80-year music manufacturing company). Community features available free without hardware. New features launched July 2025: Individual Mix, Link Posting, and Trim Audio Files.
resources.cost: $249 device (includes 2 months of service), then $9.99/mo or $95.90/yr for jamming; community features free without hardware
highlights: Each remote musician needs a Lutefish Stream device + subscription
Community networking features free without hardware
New features: Individual Mix, Link Posting, Trim Audio Files (July 2025)
Sold in the US and Canada only

resources.name: CoCreatea
resources.description: Social network for musicians and other creatives, built for collaboration. Collaborate for free, build long-term producer relationships, network across 28 music roles, and work with videographers and visual artists for music videos. Zero-commission platform. Free to join.
resources.cost: Free

resources.name: Audiomovers LISTENTO
resources.description: Collection of plugins and apps designed to stream uncompressed audio from within your DAW. Supports surround formats up to 9.1.6 Dolby Atmos on all plans, plus Apple Music spatial (binaural) rendering on Pro and above. Ideal for professional remote session monitoring and real-time listening sessions. Pro users can transmit up to 128 channels of lossless audio with 384kHz sample rate support. New Guest Pass, talkback, and video sync features added in 2025. New Business tier added.
resources.cost: Basic $12.99/mo ($99.99/yr); Pro $24.99/mo ($199.99/yr); Business $275/yr (annual only); 7-day free trial
highlights: Pro: up to 128 channels of lossless audio (upgraded from 16)
Apple Music spatial audio support (Pro tier)
New features 2025: Guest Pass, talkback, video sync

resources.name: TYFRA
resources.description: Music-specific professional network with full workflow integration — combining catalog storage, collaboration, DJ promotion analytics, charts, social networking, gig booking, contract/split management, and royalty invoicing in one platform. UK-based (prices in GBP) and still in its launch phase.
resources.cost: Free tier; paid plans from £9.99/mo
highlights: Emerging platform for indie music business 2026

resources.name: Sessionwire
resources.description: Real-time remote collaboration tool with bi-directional studio-quality audio (48 kHz stereo), integrated chat and HD video, file transfer, and a free DAW plugin suite (AAX, VST3, AU). Professional alternative to LISTENTO with added video/chat features built in. All-in-one collaborative tool for remote music production.
resources.cost: Free; paid from $12.99/mo (14-day free trial)
highlights: Free DAW plugin suite (AAX, VST3, AU)
Emerging platform for remote studio sessions
